note: This is NOT the repo's benchmark_ppl.py proxy method (which estimates PPL via text-overlap similarity against /api/generate since Ollama exposes no log-probs). dotLLM exposes true token log-probs via its own `dotllm perplexity` CLI command, so this is real cross-entropy-based perplexity, not a proxy. That command was run directly (not through this repo's Python harness) because it does not speak Ollama's or an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API - it is a first-class dotLLM CLI subcommand operating directly on the GGUF file.
command: dotnet run --project src/DotLLM.Cli -c Release -- perplexity <model.gguf> --corpus wiki.test.raw --context 512 --device cpu --max-tokens 8192

corpus.conversion: test-00000-of-00001.parquet -> concatenated text -> wiki.test.raw (standard llama.cpp-style corpus file)
corpus.subset_reason: Full wikitext-2 test set is ~290K tokens. At this hardware's measured CPU prefill throughput (~8.7 tokens/s effective for this model/backend), a full run would take on the order of 9 hours - impractical for this session. A GPU teacher-forced run was also measured (O(n^2) growing-prefix re-prefill, since the CUDA backend does not yet return all-rows logits) and was similarly slow (~10.5 tokens/s effective, and scales quadratically per window). An 8192-token genuine wikitext-2 subset was used instead as an honest, clearly-labeled partial run rather than a multi-hour full run or a synthetic fallback passage.

comparison_smoke_test.description: A smaller 2048-token CPU sliding-window smoke test (run first, to validate the command before committing to the full 8192-token run) gave PPL 13.6035 +/- 1.31034 over 1020 scored tokens - within noise of the 8192-token result given the small sample sizes and different windows sampled.

gpu_teacher_forced_probe.description: Single probe on --device cuda --mode teacher-forced (required because the CUDA backend only returns last-row logits, not all-rows, so sliding-window mode is unavailable on GPU). Included for reference only, not as the primary PPL signal, since teacher-forced mode's O(n^2) growing-prefix re-prefill only covers one context window's worth of positions.
